narrative.executive_summary: The repository demonstrates strong capabilities in CI/CD, data management, structure, and testing, with perfect scores in CI/CD, data, structure, and near-perfect testing. However, security is a significant concern, with a low score capped by critical vulnerabilities including unparameterized database queries (SEC-05@21f8627dd5d1) and numerous vulnerable dependencies (SEC-02@21f8627dd5d1). Authentication and authorization are partially enforced but have gaps, notably in some routes lacking proper authentication and authorization checks (AUTH-01@21f8627dd5d1, AUTH-03@21f8627dd5d1). Documentation and performance also show room for improvement, with low documentation coverage and missing caching and resource limits. Logging is generally well implemented but includes some use of print statements in production code (LOG-02@21f8627dd5d1).

per_metric.text: The authentication metric scores six out of ten with high coverage. Authentication is enforced on many API entrypoints, but some routes that create or modify data lack proper authentication, such as the /private/users/ endpoint (AUTH-01@21f8627dd5d1). Authorization protects privileged operations in several routes, but some privileged-capable endpoints lack authorization checks (AUTH-03@21f8627dd5d1). Passwords are securely hashed using Argon2 with a bcrypt fallback (AUTH-05@21f8627dd5d1), and tokens are validated with vetted libraries (AUTH-04@21f8627dd5d1).

The CI/CD metric achieves a perfect score with full coverage. The repository contains multiple CI workflows that run build, lint, and test steps (CI-01@21f8627dd5d1, CI-02@21f8627dd5d1). Workflows are free of actionlint errors (CI-03@21f8627dd5d1), use least-privilege permissions for tokens (CI-04@21f8627dd5d1), and pin third-party actions to commit SHAs (CI-05@21f8627dd5d1). Deployments are gated appropriately (CI-06@21f8627dd5d1), and credentials come from OIDC or secret stores (CI-07@21f8627dd5d1).

The container metric scores six and a half out of ten with full coverage. Base images are pinned in all Dockerfiles (CTR-02@21f8627dd5d1), and .dockerignore files are present (CTR-04@21f8627dd5d1). Health checks or probes are defined (CTR-05@21f8627dd5d1), and Dockerfiles are free of hadolint errors (CTR-07@21f8627dd5d1). However, containers run as root due to missing non-root USER directives in all Dockerfiles (CTR-01@21f8627dd5d1), and one Dockerfile lacks a multi-stage build (CTR-03@21f8627dd5d1).

The data metric is perfect with seventy-three percent coverage. Schema changes are managed by migrations (DATA-01@21f8627dd5d1), and connection settings come from configuration or secret stores (DATA-02@21f8627dd5d1). Multi-step writes use transactions to ensure atomicity (DATA-04@21f8627dd5d1).

Documentation scores five point seven out of ten with high coverage. The README covers the project's purpose and links to backend, frontend, and development documentation but lacks explicit setup and run commands (DOC-01@21f8627dd5d1). API documentation is generated by FastAPI (DOC-02@21f8627dd5d1), and a contributing guide and changelog are present (DOC-05@21f8627dd5d1). However, architecture documents or ADRs are missing (DOC-03@21f8627dd5d1), and docstring coverage is low at twenty-six percent (DOC-04@21f8627dd5d1).

Logging scores nine out of ten with full coverage. A logging framework is used (LOG-01@21f8627dd5d1), and request correlation with trace context is propagated via Sentry (LOG-03@21f8627dd5d1). Sensitive data is not logged (LOG-04@21f8627dd5d1), and a health check endpoint supports telemetry (LOG-05@21f8627dd5d1). However, there are some print or console output calls in production code, which is discouraged (LOG-02@21f8627dd5d1).

Performance scores five point five out of ten with full coverage. Non-blocking IO is used in request paths (PERF-01@21f8627dd5d1), and list endpoints are paginated to bound result sizes (PERF-04@21f8627dd5d1). There is no evidence of N+1 query patterns (PERF-02@21f8627dd5d1). However, the codebase lacks caching strategies for expensive reads (PERF-03@21f8627dd5d1), outbound calls such as SMTP/email lack timeouts and retries (PERF-05@21f8627dd5d1), and resource limits are not configured for any deployments (PERF-06@21f8627dd5d1).

Security scores four out of ten with full coverage and is capped by critical findings. There are twenty-one vulnerable dependencies at or above medium severity, including critical ones (SEC-02@21f8627dd5d1). Database queries are not fully parameterized, with a raw SQL query constructed via Python f-string including untrusted input, risking SQL injection (SEC-05@21f8627dd5d1). Some untrusted input is validated at system boundaries, but at least one handler uses raw query parameters without validation (SEC-04@21f8627dd5d1). CORS is safely configured with restricted origins, but common security headers are missing (SEC-06@21f8627dd5d1). Automated dependency updates are configured (SEC-07@21f8627dd5d1). No secrets are committed to the repository (SEC-01@21f8627dd5d1).

Structure scores a perfect ten out of ten with full coverage. The codebase has clear module and layer boundaries, with request handlers delegating to separate modules for data access and business logic (STR-01@21f8627dd5d1). No source files exceed one thousand lines of code (STR-02@21f8627dd5d1), function complexity is well controlled with no functions exceeding a cyclomatic complexity of fifteen (STR-03@21f8627dd5d1), and there are no circular imports between internal modules (STR-04@21f8627dd5d1). Configuration is cleanly separated from code using a Settings object (STR-05@21f8627dd5d1), and all dependency manifests are locked (STR-06@21f8627dd5d1).

Testing scores nine point one out of ten with full coverage. A test suite is present with multiple test files and tests (TEST-01@21f8627dd5d1). Test code is proportionate to source code (TEST-02@21f8627dd5d1), and tests are executed in CI (TEST-03@21f8627dd5d1). Test coverage is measured (TEST-04@21f8627dd5d1), and tests contain meaningful assertions about HTTP status, response content, and persisted state (TEST-05@21f8627dd5d1).
